articles.title: The July Visa Bulletin Just Shut the Door on India's EB-2 Green Cards. It Will Not Reopen Until October.
articles.excerpt: EB-2 India declared unavailable for the rest of FY2026, EB-1 retrogressed by two months, and EB-5 unreserved also shut — the worst mid-year bulletin for Indian professionals in years.
articles.image_caption: The U.S. State Department building in Washington, D.C. — the July 2026 Visa Bulletin has retrogressed EB-2 India to unavailable (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals in the US face frozen green card applications until October, with EB-2 declared unavailable and EB-1 retrogressing — the worst mid-year bulletin in years.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Wants Access to Anthropic's Most Powerful AI. Washington Is Listening — Carefully.
articles.excerpt: New Delhi is in talks to use Anthropic's Project Glasswing to stress-test India's critical digital infrastructure, as both countries navigate the geopolitics of frontier AI.
articles.image_caption: Frontier AI models are at the heart of US-India technology negotiations (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin AI professionals work at the heart of America's frontier AI companies; the US-India partnership on model access will determine how freely their expertise flows between both ecosystems.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Accounts Just Went Live. For Indian-American Families, the Math Is Extraordinarily Good.
articles.excerpt: The government's new $1,000 seed investment program launched on July 4. With Indian Americans among the highest-earning groups in the U.S., their families are uniquely positioned to maximize it — but only if they act fast.
articles.image_caption: The U.S. Treasury Department building in Washington, D.C., which oversees the new Trump Accounts program
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American families — among the highest-earning in the U.S. — are uniquely positioned to maximize Trump Accounts, but eligibility requires U.S. citizenship, creating a sharp distinction for H-1B families with foreign-born vs. American-born children.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hundreds of Masked White Nationalists Marched Through Washington on America's 250th Birthday. They Chanted 'Reclaim America.'
articles.excerpt: The Patriot Front's flash-mob march near the US Capitol came hours after Trump called immigrants a 'communist menace' at Mount Rushmore — a jarring backdrop for the 4.8 million Indian Americans celebrating the Fourth of July.
articles.image_caption: Patriot Front members march in formation through Washington, D.C.
articles.nri_angle: White nationalist group marches through the US capital on July 4, directly challenging the belonging of immigrant communities including the 4.8 million Indian Americans who call America home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Britain Is About to Get Its Seventh Prime Minister in a Decade. The 1.8 Million Indians There Are Watching Closely.
articles.excerpt: Andy Burnham is expected to enter Downing Street by July 20 — five days after the India-UK trade deal goes live. His domestic-first agenda could reshape life for Britain's Indian diaspora.
articles.image_caption: Andy Burnham, the incoming British Prime Minister, at an event in August 2024
articles.nri_angle: Britain's next PM takes over just as the India-UK trade deal goes live, with direct implications for 1.8 million NRIs on social security portability, worker mobility, and the future of India-UK relations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Used America’s 250th Birthday to Call Immigrants a ‘Communist Menace.’ The Diaspora Heard Every Word.
articles.excerpt: Speaking beneath Mount Rushmore on the eve of July 4, the president called for ‘newcomers’ who oppose American values to be expelled — language broad enough to alarm four million Indian Americans who built their lives here legally.
articles.image_caption: Mount Rushmore in South Dakota, where Trump delivered his July 3 speech on the eve of America's 250th birthday
articles.nri_angle: Trump's 'newcomers' rhetoric at Mount Rushmore — calling immigrants a communist menace and vowing to expel them — directly threatens the 4.8 million Indian Americans who built their lives in the US through legal immigration channels.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America's 250th Birthday Was the Hottest on Record. Literally.
articles.excerpt: A historic heat dome cancelled parades from Philadelphia to Boston, strained power grids to the breaking point, and forced Trump's Great American State Fair to temporarily shut its gates.
articles.image_caption: Crowds gather on the National Mall in Washington, D.C. for Fourth of July celebrations near the Washington Monument
articles.nri_angle: Millions of Indian Americans across the East Coast and Mid-Atlantic faced cancelled celebrations and power outages during one of the community's most visible American holiday weekends.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Own Attorney General Called E20 Fuel an 'Experiment.' The Government Spent the Next 48 Hours in Damage Control.
articles.excerpt: A viral courtroom video has turned simmering consumer anger over mandatory ethanol-blended petrol into the Modi government's biggest domestic headache this summer.
articles.image_caption: A BPCL petrol pump in India, where E20 ethanol-blended fuel is now the only option at nearly all stations
articles.nri_angle: NRIs driving in India face the same E20 fuel with no alternative, and the auto sector uncertainty affects diaspora investments in one of India's flagship industries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and Japan Just Signed Their First Defence Co-Development Deal. It Is the Start of Something Much Bigger.
articles.excerpt: Modi and Takaichi summit in New Delhi delivered pacts on AI, stealth naval tech, critical minerals, and a $61 billion investment roadmap — reshaping what the two economies mean to each other.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi at the ceremonial welcome at Rashtrapati Bhavan during the 16th India-Japan Annual Summit
articles.nri_angle: With 1,400 Japanese firms already in India, a 10 trillion yen investment target, and new openings in AI and defence manufacturing, the summit creates direct job and investment pathways for NRI professionals and investors eyeing the India-Japan corridor.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Eight Men Arrested for Stealing Donations From the Ram Mandir. A Court Is Being Asked to Call In the CBI.
articles.excerpt: CCTV footage, property raids, and a PIL seeking a CAG audit — the embezzlement scandal at Ayodhya's most sacred site is deepening by the day.
articles.image_caption: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir in Ayodhya, consecrated by Prime Minister Modi in January 2024
articles.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs donated to the Ram Mandir construction fund, making this a deeply personal scandal for the diaspora — a PIL in the Allahabad High Court now seeks an independent CAG audit of the Trust's finances.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America Turns 250 Tomorrow. No Immigrant Community Has Risen Faster Than Indian Americans.
articles.excerpt: As the U.S. marks its semiquincentennial, 5.2 million Indian Americans — now the country's largest Asian ethnic group — are reshaping everything from the C-suite to Capitol Hill. Their story is also getting more complicated.
articles.image_caption: July Fourth celebrations at a U.S. Embassy, marking Independence Day
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans are now the largest Asian ethnic group in the US and pay 5-6% of all income taxes despite being 1.5% of the population — the 250th anniversary is as much their celebration as anyone's.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Operation Amistad Wins Hearts in Earthquake-Shattered Venezuela
articles.excerpt: Two IAF C-17 Globemasters, 41 medical personnel, and indigenous BHISHM cubes — India's disaster-relief machine reaches Latin America as the death toll crosses 2,600.
articles.image_caption: An Indian Air Force aircraft being loaded with humanitarian relief supplies for deployment. India's C-17 Globemasters have become the backbone of its disaster-response operations worldwide.
articles.image_credit: Indian Air Force / Government of India (GODL-India), via Wikimedia Commons
articles.nri_angle: India's growing first-responder reputation across continents reinforces national pride for the diaspora and underscores New Delhi's expanding strategic engagement with Latin America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Logged Its Driest June in Fifteen Years. The Next Two Weeks Will Decide What Millions of Farmers Eat.
articles.excerpt: Kharif sowing is running 23% behind last year, El Niño is strengthening, and food prices are already climbing. The monsoon's July performance will shape inflation and rural incomes for months to come.
articles.image_caption: Parched farmland during a delayed monsoon in India (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: A weak monsoon means higher food bills for families receiving NRI remittances, and potential rice export curbs that would affect diaspora communities in the Middle East and Southeast Asia.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Was Personally Invited to Khamenei's Funeral. India Sent a Deputy Minister Instead.
articles.excerpt: As Iran stages a week of mass processions for its slain Supreme Leader, India's carefully calibrated delegation reveals the diplomatic tightrope New Delhi walks between Tehran and Washington.
articles.image_caption: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in an official portrait released during Nowruz celebrations
articles.nri_angle: The India-Iran relationship affects Strait of Hormuz negotiations, oil prices, and shipping routes that directly impact NRIs in the Gulf and Indian businesses across the Middle East.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Scrapped Taxes on Its Bonds. $3.4 Billion Poured In Within Weeks.
articles.excerpt: New Delhi's most aggressive capital-market reform in years has unlocked record foreign inflows, and Bloomberg's biggest bond index could be next.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India building in Kolkata, home to the central bank that broadened bond access for foreign investors
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors and the broader diaspora benefit directly from a more accessible, tax-free Indian bond market — and Bloomberg index inclusion would further deepen the pool of rupee-denominated assets available for offshore portfolios.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Biggest Trade Deal Goes Live in Twelve Days. Here's What Changes for the Diaspora.
articles.excerpt: The India-UK CETA eliminates tariffs on 99 percent of Indian exports, opens 137 service sectors, and ends double social security payments for 75,000 professionals. It enters force on July 15.
articles.image_caption: UK Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds and India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal sign the India-UK trade agreement

sources.label: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

articles.nri_angle: The Double Contribution Convention ending dual social security payments directly saves Indian professionals in the UK thousands of pounds annually, while 1,800 visas for chefs, yoga instructors, and musicians create new mobility pathways.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Adani and Abu Dhabi Are Building a $11.5 Billion Aluminium Complex in Odisha. It Would Be India's Biggest Foreign Metals Investment Ever.
articles.excerpt: The 50:50 joint venture with the UAE's IHC will produce 2 million metric tons of aluminium a year, create 53,500 jobs, and raise India's smelting capacity by half. The announcement comes as a US judge keeps Adani's criminal case alive.
articles.image_caption: Gautam Adani, chairman of the Adani Group
articles.nri_angle: The massive Gulf-India industrial tie-up signals deepening economic integration between India and the UAE, while the US court proceedings over Adani's alleged bribery scheme remain a governance concern for NRI investors holding Adani Group securities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Is Heading to Three Countries Next Week. In One of Them, Indians Are Being Told They're Not Welcome.
articles.excerpt: The PM's six-day tour covers Indonesia, Australia and New Zealand — where a historic first visit in 40 years collides with anti-Indian immigration crackdowns and planned protests.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese at a bilateral meeting
articles.nri_angle: One million Indian-born Australians, 250,000 Indians in New Zealand, and a historic PM visit colliding with targeted anti-Indian immigration rules make this tour deeply personal for the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foreign Money Is Leaving India's Stock Market at a Record Pace. For the First Time in Two Decades, Indian Investors Don't Need It.
articles.excerpt: The RBI's latest Financial Stability Report reveals FPI ownership at a 20-year low of 16%, with domestic investors commanding 20% — and new rules now let NRIs own even more.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building on Dalal Street, Mumbai — the epicentre of India's equity markets where domestic investors now hold more sway than foreign funds for the first time in two decades.
articles.nri_angle: RBI raised equity investment limits for NRIs and OCIs as part of measures to attract overseas capital, giving the diaspora broader access to Indian markets at corrected valuations
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Services Engine Just Hit Its Slowest Speed in Seventeen Months. The Hiring Freeze Is the Bigger Story.
articles.excerpt: The HSBC India Services PMI fell to 57.4 in June as domestic demand weakened sharply and only 1% of firms added staff — a dramatic retreat from the hiring boom of April and May.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, India's financial capital
articles.nri_angle: A weakening services sector in India directly threatens the IT outsourcing industry that employs millions of NRIs and underpins H-1B visa sponsorship pipelines to the US, UK and Canada.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI Hiring in India Just Surged 16%. The Rest of the IT Industry Is Shrinking.
articles.excerpt: A Naukri report shows AI roles grew 16% year-on-year in June while overall IT jobs fell 3% — the clearest sign yet that India's $315 billion tech sector is splitting into two economies.
articles.image_caption: Aerial view of the glass pyramid at the Infosys campus in Bangalore, India's IT capital
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT professionals on H-1B visas work disproportionately in the traditional services roles being automated — the AI-versus-IT split directly shapes their career security and immigration prospects.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Let Four Chinese Power Equipment Firms Bid for Government Contracts. Five Years of Frozen Relations Are Thawing Fast.
articles.excerpt: A Finance Ministry order gives TBEA Energy, Nanjing Electric India and two other Chinese-linked manufacturers a two-year exemption to compete for critical power tenders — the latest in a calibrated reset with Beijing.
articles.image_caption: An electrical power substation in Sambalpur, Odisha, India
articles.nri_angle: NRIs in U.S. energy and infrastructure sectors should watch the India-China power equipment thaw closely — it reshapes both the competitive landscape and collaboration opportunities in India's energy transition.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: CRED's Kunal Shah Is Now Running WhatsApp. Meta Paid $900 Million to Make It Happen.
articles.excerpt: The Indian founder who turned credit card bills into a fintech empire now leads the world's biggest messaging app. It's the most consequential Indian tech appointment since Satya Nadella.
articles.image_caption: Kunal Shah, founder of CRED and newly appointed global head of WhatsApp (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: An Indian founder — not an Indian-American corporate executive — now leads the platform that is the primary communication channel between the diaspora and home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Has Now Served Notices to Every Major Messaging App Over Usernames. The Crackdown Is Widening.
articles.excerpt: After freezing WhatsApp's username rollout, the government is now demanding answers from Telegram and Signal. Indian platform Arattai has already surrendered the feature entirely.
articles.image_caption: A user texting on WhatsApp, India's dominant messaging platform with over 500 million users
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora Indians who rely on WhatsApp, Telegram, and Signal to communicate with family could see privacy features limited if India forces platforms to tie usernames to verified phone numbers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Opened Its Nuclear Sector to Private Money for the First Time in Sixty Years. The $214 Billion Race Is On.
articles.excerpt: The SHANTI Act lets Adani, Tata, and Jindal build nuclear power plants. IIT Bombay is already training the engineers. And the West is watching closely.
articles.image_caption: The Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant in Tamil Nadu, India's largest nuclear power station
articles.nri_angle: The 49% FDI window means diaspora-led investment and Indian-origin nuclear engineers at US firms like Westinghouse now have a professional pathway into India's nuclear sector.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Refiners Are Redrawing the Oil Map. The Iran War Forced Their Hand.
articles.excerpt: Indian Oil, BPCL and HPCL are eyeing crude from Guyana, Brazil and the US to reduce their dependence on the Middle East — a shift that could be the most significant in India's energy history.
articles.image_caption: An oil refinery in India — the country's refiners are reshaping crude supply chains after the Iran war disrupted Gulf shipping routes (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: India's crude oil import bill is the single biggest variable in the country's fiscal equation — affecting the rupee, inflation, petrol prices and government spending capacity. A structural shift in sourcing from the Gulf to the Americas and Africa would reshape India's economic risk profile for years.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's GST Revenue Just Hit ₹1.95 Lakh Crore in a Single Month. The Real Story Is in the Imports.
articles.excerpt: Gross collections rose 14% year-on-year in June, powered by a 35% spike in import-linked taxes — a signal of surging trade that cuts both ways for the economy.
articles.image_caption: India's GST collections have become a key barometer of economic health
articles.nri_angle: GST collections are the most reliable real-time measure of India's economic health — the June numbers show both steady domestic consumption and a massive ramp-up in capital goods imports as global firms build manufacturing and data infrastructure.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America Just Added Its Fewest Jobs Since February. India’s IT Stocks Are Rallying.
articles.excerpt: The U.S. economy created only 57,000 jobs in June — roughly half what Wall Street expected. The weak print has pushed back rate-hike fears, sent the dollar tumbling, and given Indian markets their strongest week in months.
articles.image_caption: The trading floor at the New York Stock Exchange on Wall Street
articles.nri_angle: The weak U.S. jobs report eases rate-hike fears, stabilises the rupee, and lifts Indian IT stocks — directly affecting NRI employment prospects, mortgage costs, and the India-vs-America career calculus.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi Just Banned New Petrol Two-Wheelers From 2028. No Indian City Has Gone This Far.
articles.excerpt: India’s capital has launched its most aggressive electric vehicle policy yet — ₹15,000 crore in incentives, 30,000 new charging points, and a hard deadline that will force every new scooter buyer to go electric within two years.
articles.image_caption: An electric vehicle charging station at NITI Aayog in New Delhi
articles.nri_angle: Delhi’s EV push could improve the air quality that keeps NRIs from moving back, while opening investment opportunities in India’s booming electric vehicle supply chain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: HCLTech Just Landed a $1.14 Billion AI Deal With a European Giant. It's the Biggest New Contract in Years.
articles.excerpt: The Noida-headquartered IT services firm will build an AI-driven operating model for a major unnamed European company — entirely new business, not a renewal.
articles.image_caption: HCLTech CEO C Vijayakumar, who has steered the company's pivot toward AI-led transformation services
articles.nri_angle: HCLTech employs tens of thousands of Indian-origin engineers in the US and Europe — a mega deal of this size signals continued demand for Indian tech talent globally.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Sending Its Top Trade Bodies to Washington Next Week. They're Going to Fight a $30 Billion Tariff.
articles.excerpt: FICCI, CII, the Commerce Ministry and three industry associations will testify before the USTR on July 8, arguing that America's forced-labour findings are legally flawed and economically destructive.
articles.image_caption: The Winder Building in Washington, D.C., headquarters of the Office of the United States Trade Representative

sources.label: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

articles.nri_angle: If the 12.5% tariff takes effect, it could raise prices on Indian goods in the US, disrupt supply chains that employ diaspora professionals, and complicate the bilateral trade deal that affects everything from H-1B policies to student visa reciprocity.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Just Handed India's Government Its Biggest Cheque Ever. Here's Why It Matters.
articles.excerpt: A record ₹2.87 lakh crore dividend — earned largely from defending the rupee during the Iran war — has compressed India's fiscal deficit to just 9.6% of the full-year target in two months. But the real test lies ahead.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai

sources.label: Reserve Bank of India Annual Report FY26

articles.nri_angle: India's fiscal health directly affects rupee stability, bond yields and the investment climate that NRIs navigate for remittances, property and portfolio decisions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Canada Is Spending $500 Billion on Defence. It Wants India to Help Build the Arsenal.
articles.excerpt: From expelled diplomats to a full defence dialogue in four months — Canada and India are engineering one of the fastest diplomatic turnarounds in recent memory, with a free trade deal and a Modi visit to Ottawa on the horizon.
articles.image_caption: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, who has spearheaded a dramatic reset in India-Canada relations since taking office
articles.nri_angle: The India-Canada reset directly affects nearly two million Indian-Canadians through improved visa processing, trade corridors, security cooperation and the political normalisation of a relationship that had turned hostile under Trudeau.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's First Private Rocket Is Ten Days From Orbit. The Startup Behind It Just Became a Unicorn.
articles.excerpt: Skyroot Aerospace has set a July 12 launch window for Vikram-1, aiming to become only the fourth private company in the world to place a satellite in orbit from its own launch vehicle.
articles.image_caption: Skyroot's Vikram-S rocket during Mission Prarambh at Sriharikota in November 2022
articles.nri_angle: Indian space startups are opening a new pathway for diaspora investors and technologists to participate in India's $44 billion commercial space economy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
